                                      PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                          §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                       §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                    §                   OF TEXAS

                    ELECTRIC TRANSMISSION TEXAS, LLC’S COMMENTS
                          ON STAFF’S 2ND DISCUSSION DRAFT

        Electric Transmission Texas, LLC (ETT) is a transmission-only joint venture between

American Electric Power Company, Inc. and Berkshire Hathaway Energy. ETT respectfully

submits these comments in response to Staff’s 2nd Discussion Draft filed January 2, 2026, and the

discussion during the January 9, 2026 Commission Workshop (Workshop) regarding large load

interconnection standards under PURA § 37.0561.


Definition of Interconnecting Utility

        A singular definition of Interconnecting Utility is not sufficient to address the complexity

associated with interconnecting a large load entity. As discussed in the Workshop, there can be

multiple parties involved to interconnect a large load and additional complexities depending on

the specific configuration of the facilities. The rule language specifies responsibilities regarding

the load interconnection that are assigned to the Interconnecting Utility. However, utilizing one

definition of Interconnecting Utility creates substantial challenges to consider when the

interconnecting Transmission Service Provider (TSP) differs from the certificated delivery

provider and raises additional questions when the load serving utility can designate to a TSP that

is a transmission-only utility.

        Assigning Interconnecting Utility responsibilities to a transmission-only utility could

introduce new reporting and compliance obligations that these entities are neither structured to

                                                 1
 meet nor currently required to perform. Some specific considerations from the perspective of a

transmission-only utility include, but are not limited to:

           Transmission-only tariffs may not include the typical language that Transmission

            Distribution Service Provider (TDSP) tariffs contain with respect to load

            interconnections and Contributions In Aid of Construction (CIAC). Unless the rule

            language is entirely specific regarding CIAC for large load interconnections, the

            existing Commission-approved transmission-only utility tariffs may not adequately

            address or support the additional responsibilities outlined in this discussion draft.

           Transmission-only utilities do not currently report load data or provide responses to the

            Annual Load Data Request (ALDR) process at ERCOT.

           The discussion draft raises questions about who could own the breakers used to connect

            and disconnect load at the Service Delivery Point because ETT does not provide retail

            delivery service and does not have a certificated service territory.

           ETT does not receive a load-shed order in the instance of an Energy Emergency Alert

            issuance. ETT is uncertain what this emergency process would be if another utility

            designated it as an Interconnecting Utility.


Conclusion

        ETT appreciates the opportunity to provide comments in this proceeding and looks forward

to working with Commission Staff and other parties to further evaluate these issues and develop

potential solutions. ETT further appreciates the Commission’s consideration of these comments.

An executive summary of the comments is provided as the last page of this filing.
